Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finserv.com>, FinServe Legal <legal@finserv.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA redlines: EU-only processing, retention windows, audit rights

Priya —

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. Our Legal team reviewed the standard DPA and came back with a set of redlines attached (FinServe_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx). The key asks are below and we'd like to understand Redwood's position:

1) EU-only processing: All customer content, metadata, and related logs must be stored and processed within the EU. No cross-border transfers except with explicit written consent.

2) Retention & deletion: Customer content must be deleted within 90 days of account termination or written request. Audit logs necessary for billing/compliance may be retained up to 12 months but must remain in the EU.

3) Subprocessors: We require a list of subprocessors responsible for data handling and a 30-day notice for any changes.

4) Audit & attestations: FinServe requires the right to audit high-risk controls (either onsite or via a third-party auditor) annually. SOC 2 reports alone are not sufficient in all cases.

Please let us know which items Redwood can accept as-is, which require alternative language, and whether these changes will affect deployment mode/pricing.

Attached: FinServe_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx (redlines)

Best,
Megan

Subject: Re: DPA redlines: EU-only processing, retention windows, audit rights

Priya / team — reviewed FinServe redlines. My notes and suggested compromise language below. Attaching a plain-text patch with line-level suggestions (DPA_clause_suggestions.txt). High-level:

- EU-only processing: We can commit to EU-only processing for Customer Content and Customer Identifiers when the customer uses our EU-hosted region (eu-west-1). For hosted customers using global routing, we propose: "Customer Data will be processed and stored in the EU when the Customer requests EU-only hosting and still subject to Redwood's documented high-availability fallback policy." We also propose a clause that allows temporary cross-border processing for resilience if needed, with prior notice and the customer can require Private deployment for strict EU residency.

Operational impact: EU-only hosting requires either Hosted API pinned to EU region (no cross-region replication) or Dedicated/Private deployment. This can increase cost ~10-20% (depending on throughput).

- Retention & deletion: We cannot commit to a 90-day deletion for all system logs without clarifying log types. Proposed breakdown:
  * Customer Content (messages, files, model outputs): deleted within 30 days of termination/request, unless customer requests longer retention.
  * Audit/Billing Logs (billing records, access logs tied to invoices): retained up to 12 months, stored in EU when EU-hosting is selected.
  * System telemetry and aggregated telemetry (non-identifying) — 180 days.

Technical notes: For deletion we can provide API-triggered purge and documented deletion timelines plus KMS key rotation to enforce crypto-deletion for private deployments. For Hosted customers, we can schedule a data purge job and provide deletion certificates.

- Subprocessors: We can provide a current subprocessor list and commit to 30-day notice for material changes. For certain cloud infra providers (major CSPs), we request allowed exception language (standard infra provider rules).

- Audit rights: We generally provide SOC 2 reports and allow in-person audits for Dedicated/Private customers under a mutual NDA and pre-scheduled window. For Hosted customers, SOC 2 + security questionnaires are our standard. Onsite or deep-dive audits for Hosted customers would require a scope definition and cost recovery.

Suggested quick reply to FinServe: offer the EU-only hosting commitment if they select EU-hosted region or Dedicated capacity; propose the retention breakdown above; provide subprocessor list and 30-day notice commitment; propose SOC 2 + option for an annual third-party audit for Dedicated customers. Ask for FinServe's priority items and whether they're willing to accept Private/Dedicated mode for stricter residency/audit needs.

Attachment: DPA_clause_suggestions.txt (line-level suggested text and alternatives).

If this looks good I'll draft a clean redline to send back to Megan and include legal to finalize.

— Dev
Senior Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Sato <megan.sato@finserv.com>

Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: EU-only processing, retention windows, audit rights

Megan —

Thanks for the redlines and for laying out FinServe's priorities. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromises to move towards agreement:

1) EU processing: Redwood will commit to processing and storing Customer Content and Customer Identifiers in the EU for customers who select our EU-hosted region or who deploy on Redwood Dedicated/Private. For Hosted customers choosing global routing, we will:
   - Route and store primary customer content in the EU when the EU-hosting option is selected.
   - Allow temporary, limited cross-border processing for failover only, with prior written notice where feasible.
   - If FinServe requires strict contractual EU-only assurance with no cross-border exception, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment and we will reflect that in the DPA.

2) Retention & deletion: Proposed retention windows (we can include these as specific DPA clauses):
   - Customer Content (e.g., messages, uploaded files, model outputs): deletion within 30 days of termination or upon documented deletion request, unless customer explicitly requests extended retention.
   - Billing and invoice-related records: retained up to 12 months for billing reconciliation, stored in EU when EU-hosting is selected.
   - Audit logs that include identifying info (access logs tied to users): retained up to 12 months.
   - Aggregated/telemetry (non-identifying): retained up to 180 days.

We will provide a deletion certificate for Customer Content deletions and offer API-based purge for programmatic control. For Private deployments, we can support KMS-based crypto-delete proofs.

3) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor list and commit to 30-day notice for material additions. Standard infrastructure providers (CSPs) will be listed and treated as subprocessors with the standard carve-outs described in the DPA.

4) Audit & attestations: For Hosted customers we provide SOC 2 Type II and detailed security questionnaires. For Dedicated/Private customers we can agree to an annual third-party audit or onsite review under an NDA and with mutually-agreed scope. Onsite audits for Hosted customers will need scope and cost conversation.

Next steps: Attached is a clean PDF with our proposed redlines (redwood_proposed_dpa_redlines.pdf). If this is acceptable as a starting point, can we schedule a short legal call (30 minutes) this week to walk through the remaining items? I've proposed a DocuSign stub for an NDA or audit addendum if needed: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC12345.

If you prefer, we can also put together a Dedicated capacity quote that prices the EU-only guarantee and onsite audit option.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0199
